repository.name: oppia
repository.description: A free, online learning platform to make quality education accessible for all.

issue.body:
## Summary
- Migrates `translation-coordinator/manage-contributors-translation-review-rights` from Puppeteer to Playwright.
- Ports the contributor admin, contributor, translation coordinator, translation submitter, and translation reviewer utilities needed by the migrated spec.
- Moves the existing screenshot baselines into the Playwright snapshot layout and routes the suite to Playwright in `acceptance.json`.

## Issue
Fixes #26840.

## Validation
- `core\tests\playwright-acceptance-tests\node_modules\.bin\tsc.cmd --noEmit --ignoreDeprecations 5.0 -p core\tests\playwright-acceptance-tests\tsconfig.json`
- `node -e "JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('core/tests/ci-test-suite-configs/acceptance.json','utf8'))"`
- `git diff --cached --check`

I could not complete the local desktop/mobile acceptance run in native Windows because Oppia's local installer explicitly requires WSL/Linux and the runner fails before reaching the test while starting infrastructure. I will run the GitHub Actions stress test from the fork for the required desktop/mobile coverage.

It adds a role-specific utility `TranslationCoordinator` under `core/tests/playwright-acceptance-tests/utilities/user/translation-coordinator.ts`, maps `ROLES.TRANSLATION_COORDINATOR` in `user-factory.ts`, and updates all component interactions and selectors to match Playwright standards.

GSoC 2027 is approaching! This tracker lists meaningful, well-scoped issues to help prospective contributors get familiar with the codebase, development workflow, and different areas of the project while making useful contributions.

> [!NOTE]
> **Before contributing:** Please read the [Contributing Code to Oppia](https://github.com/oppia/oppia/wiki/Contributing-code-to-Oppia#setting-things-up) guide and set up your development environment.
>
> Contributing to these issues does not guarantee GSoC selection. The goal is to build familiarity with the project and make meaningful contributions.

## How to Contribute

1. Browse the issues listed below and choose one that matches your experience and interests.
2. Comment with your proposed approach, files you expect to modify, and, if possible, a short demo.
3. Wait for maintainer review and assignment.
4. Once assigned, submit a PR following the project's contribution guidelines.
5. As you gain experience, take on more challenging issues and explore areas of the project in depth.

> [!CAUTION]
> **Strict note on AI usage**
>
> We expect all contributors to understand and take ownership of their contributions, including emails, comments, issue discussions, and PRs. AI tools can be valuable aids for learning, debugging, and coding, provided they are used responsibly with meaningful understanding. As a good rule of thumb, you should always be able to explain in detail what your code does and why the way it’s written is correct.
>
> Our reviewers and maintainers volunteer their time, and their time is valuable. Low-effort AI-generated contributions create unnecessary review overhead and take time away from helping genuine contributors.
>
> Contributors who repeatedly submit low-effort or AI-generated content without understanding it will receive warnings. Continued violations may result in a ban from contributing to the project.
